nodes.summary: For a prior `p` on the finite set of type profiles and utilities `u i θ o` that may depend on the whole type profile, the expected utility of agent `i` of type `θi` when each profile `θ` leads to the outcome `h θ`: `∑_{θ : θ i = θi} p θ · u i θ (h θ)`. This is Myerson's `Zᵢ` (1979, equation (5)) multiplied by the marginal probability of `θi`, so the incentive constraints below are those of Myerson (1979, (6))…
nodes.title: Interim expected utility

nodes.summary: In a private-values model, a dominant-strategy incentive-compatible direct mechanism is Bayesian incentive compatible for every nonnegative prior `p`.
nodes.title: Strategy-proof mechanisms are Bayesian incentive compatible

nodes.summary: The direct mechanism `f` is Bayesian incentive compatible: truthful reporting is a Bayesian Nash equilibrium, that is, no agent of any type `θi` gains in interim expectation by reporting `θi'` while the others report truthfully (Myerson 1979, (6); Myerson 1981, (3.5); Myerson and Satterthwaite 1983, §2).
nodes.title: Bayesian incentive compatibility

nodes.summary: In a private-values model (agent `i`'s utility `w i (θ i) o` depends only on its own type), a profile of dominant strategies is a Bayesian Nash equilibrium for every nonnegative prior `p`.
nodes.title: Dominant strategies are Bayesian Nash

nodes.summary: The pure strategy profile `s` is a Bayesian Nash equilibrium of the mechanism `g` for the prior `p` and the utilities `u`: no agent of any type gains in interim expectation by a unilateral deviation to another action, the others following `s` (Myerson 1979, (14), restricted to pure response plans).
nodes.title: Bayesian Nash equilibrium

nodes.summary: The direct mechanism `f`, which maps each profile of reported types to an outcome, is dominant-strategy incentive compatible (strategy-proof): truthful reporting is optimal for every agent whatever the others report (Nisan 2007, Definition 9.15, with payments absorbed into the outcome).
nodes.title: Dominant-strategy incentive compatibility

nodes.summary: In the mechanism `g`, with private-value utilities `u i θᵢ o`, the strategy profile `s` (agent `i` of type `θᵢ` plays `s i θᵢ`) is a profile of dominant strategies: whatever the others play, `s i θᵢ` is a best action for agent `i` of type `θᵢ` (Nisan 2007, Definition 9.24 and the definition of dominant-strategy implementation in §9.4.2).
nodes.title: Dominant-strategy profile

nodes.summary: If `s` is a profile of dominant strategies in the mechanism `g`, then at every type profile `θ` the action profile `fun j ↦ s j (θ j)` is a pure Nash equilibrium of the complete-information game with costs `-u i (θ i) (g x)` (`PotentialGame.IsPureNash` is stated for costs).
nodes.title: Dominant strategies give pure Nash equilibria

nodes.summary: If the pure strategies `s` form a Bayesian Nash equilibrium of the mechanism `g`, then the direct mechanism `θ ↦ g (fun j ↦ s j (θ j))` is Bayesian incentive compatible, and by construction its truthful outcome at every type profile is the equilibrium outcome of `g`, so every type of every agent gets the same interim utility (Myerson 1979, Theorem 2; Myerson 1981, Lemma 1). Myerson's Theorem 2 also allows…
nodes.title: Revelation principle (Bayesian, pure strategies)

nodes.summary: If the strategies `s` form a profile of dominant strategies in the mechanism `g`, then the direct mechanism `θ ↦ g (fun j ↦ s j (θ j))` is dominant-strategy incentive compatible; by construction its truthful outcome at every type profile is the equilibrium outcome of `g` (Nisan 2007, Proposition 9.25; payments are part of the outcome, so they agree as well).
nodes.title: Revelation principle (dominant strategies)

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
